- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.2) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.1) — model underreacts to bearish signals.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes; correct by reducing forecast peak values by 5–10% after a spike.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds too much upward momentum; apply downward correction in later days if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model often fails to capture early mean reversion — adjust by adding 1–2 days of downward drift after peak.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, reduce forecast volatility — avoid sharp swings in middle-to-late horizon.
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum early, model tends to overcorrect later — apply a “cool-down” factor to later forecast days.
